betterruins:Ahh I see I will try to get: Ahh I see I will try to get you those gears and return.
betterruins:All the finest soldiers’ tom: All the finest soldiers’ tombs are adorned by those ceremonial weapons of silver and gold, so, must mean you’re a pretty capable warrior if you can get your hands on something like that. I want you to give me a scythe forged of solid gold, and then I will share with you the location of this pit. It’d be impractical as a tool, of course! But oh, how fun! I can already see it, hanging upon the hearth... and the look on my colleagues’ face when I show up with it in tow will be more valuable than anything gears can buy.
betterruins:And one more thing. Don't ex: And one more thing. Don't expect answers from the map - just observe the things around you, that always helped me in difficult situations like yours.
betterruins:And would you like to visit: And would you like to visit it?
betterruins:Another tragic story? I don': Another tragic story? I don't have time.
betterruins:As they say: as they flared: As they say: as they flared up, so they faded. As far as I know, it's unlikely anyone has forced themselves to visit that place again. After the terrible rumors that spread through the world following their failure. I even think a tradition appeared to leave that place alone.
betterruins:Can you remind me where the: [BR Quest] Can you remind me where the location with the sun symbol was?
betterruins:Don’t you fret. I thought th: Don’t you fret. I thought this might happen, so I kept another copy on hand. You Seraphs ought to stop making up stories about having died far-away every single time you misplace your things.
betterruins:Eager, are you? Wise or fool: Eager, are you? Wise or foolish - we shall see. This map leads to a chamber beneath the sands, once known as the Crossroads Below. Vaulted stone, buried secrets. It's not marked by stone, but by silence - and silence keeps its secrets well.
betterruins:Hard to imagine how it ended: Hard to imagine how it ended...
betterruins:Heard you... unpleasant, I'l: Heard you... unpleasant, I'll think about it.
betterruins:Here you go I got another co: Here you go I got another copy of the map.
betterruins:Here’s your map, and best of:
Here’s your map, and best of luck on your journey.

Give my regards to that old friend of mine when you get there, will you?
betterruins:I agree with you. Let's leav: I agree with you. Let's leave that place be.
betterruins:I don't really want to break: I don't really want to break tradition. And it's quite far - I trust rumors more than my own cart for such a distance. Yet safety comes first, it's no place for me alone. They also say danger outlives its masters.
betterruins:I guess they are. I won’t pr: I guess they are. I won’t pry further.
betterruins:I have the pickaxe in exchan: [BR Quest] I have the pickaxe in exchange for the map with the sun.
[BR Quest] I lost that map you gave me.
betterruins:I lost the map to the Halite: I lost the map to the Halite Quarry!
betterruins:I suppose poor taste can’t b: I suppose poor taste can’t be helped.
betterruins:I think I have a map from th: I think I have a map from there... I'm not sure it leads exactly to it, but the mark with the sun suggests otherwise. The sun - the symbol of that place...
betterruins:I understand, do you have an: I understand, do you have anything else?
betterruins:I want to obtain it. I assum: I want to obtain it. I assume you need something in return?
betterruins:I'll stick to the map, thank: I'll stick to the map, thank you very much.
betterruins:I'll try to satisfy your req: I'll try to satisfy your request to prove my intentions.
Is there one? Not too old.
I’ll see what I can do.
betterruins:I’ll tell you, but I need to: I’ll tell you, but I need to be sure that you know how to put together a quern or you’ll be left with useless halite stone. Conveniently, I’ve also gotten very bored of the dull granite grey of my own quern. You work on bringing me one with a prettier colour and I’ll work on drawing you up a map. Andesite, basalt, peridotite, a quern carved from any of those three would do.
betterruins:I’m looking forward to it. I: I’m looking forward to it. I’ll have the map ready when you return.
betterruins:I’m sure I simply don’t appr: I’m sure I simply don’t appreciate Seraph cuisine.
betterruins:I’m sure you already have a:
I’m sure you already have a cellar to keep your foodstuffs out of the sun. When I’m travelling around local farmsteads to stock up, though, I don’t quite have that luxury.

It’s salt! If you use enough of it it tastes better, too. Cured meats, pickled veggies…
I pass by this salt mine on occasion during my travels and always take some to top off my supply.
It’s been abandoned since long before I first set foot there, so I’m sure they don’t mind.
betterruins:Lost it already? Hah. No mat: Lost it already? Hah. No matter - here, take another. Try not to feed this one to the wind.
betterruins:Maybe you should get rid of: Maybe you should get rid of it, might be safer for both of us.
betterruins:More of a quarry, really. Ha:
More of a quarry, really. Halite. Gorgeous pink stone. I’ve tried to use it for bowls to no avail, the stuff dissolves in liquids. But if you grind it up you get salt. As for the site itself, it’s full of decrepit buildings that I personally take wide berths around. Leave it to the treasure hunter types to get trapped in collapsing ruins.

I don’t think you could exhaust its reserves if you tried, so I feel comfortable sharing its location with you. I’ve seen folks like you running up to my storefront scarfing down ten or so uncooked carrots in a single sitting. So it would bring me comfort knowing that you’ve got salt available, at the very least.
betterruins:Of course... I see... yes, t: Of course... I see... yes, the pickaxe is solid. I think I can trust you with more than just the map.
betterruins:Oh, I shudder to imagine how: Oh, I shudder to imagine how deep you must’ve dug to get your hands on all that precious gold... or how much time you must’ve spent sifting it from sandy shores. Well. Whether you’re strong enough to survive the lowest reaches of this world or patient enough to tread with utmost caution, either trait will serve you well when you head into that ruin. You’ve more than proven yourself as far as I’m concerned.
betterruins:Oh, it’ll look great in my k: Oh, it’ll look great in my kitchen! Thank you kindly for your service, and here’s your map, as promised. I’m very thankful to have been a part of your culinary journey.
betterruins:Oh, look around you! What is: Oh, look around you! What isn’t noteworthy around here? Nature is thriving and providing for all of us, even amidst the surge of cursed ones plaguing these lands. You adventuring types ought to sit still and appreciate that from time to time. You remind me of my colleague, who calls themself a treasure hunter. Recently sent me a letter about some discovery they lacked the manpower to unearth. Fool’s errands, all in all. I just wish they’d take the hint and accept that some things are best left buried.
betterruins:Oh, quiet your yammering. Of:
Oh, quiet your yammering. Of course it will be. Matter of fact, it already is!
You’ve made me very happy. Honestly, can’t think of anything more worthwhile than that.
If you want to make me even happier, though, my storefront’s open...?
betterruins:Save it for now, I'll come b: Save it for now, I'll come back later.
betterruins:See, there’s somebody with a:
See, there’s somebody with a good head on their shoulders.
There are exceptions to the rule, of course. Parsnips, onions, carrots... I could go on.
Why don’t you buy some?
betterruins:Seen anything noteworthy aro: [BR Quest] Seen anything noteworthy around here lately?
betterruins:So I did. They described it: So I did. They described it as a perfectly spherical crater left behind in the landscape, with dozens of sprawling tunnels opening into that pit. Said it was infested with drifters and the likes and didn’t want to take any chances, so they asked me to send any capable warriors their way. But what do they think little old me knows about fighting? I’d certainly not dare invite you to spar. No, I reckon I’ll trade the location to you, for a very specific price.
Sounds grim, my condolences. I should go.
betterruins:Sounds worthy, but I still n: Sounds worthy, but I still need to learn that.
betterruins:Spoken like one born of purp: Spoken like one born of purpose. But rusty gears is not enough, not for this. I require something rarer - something that fell from the stars. Bring me a knife of meteoric iron. Freshly forged. Untouched by blood or rust. Only then shall I entrust you with the map.
betterruins:Strange for you to request s: Strange for you to request something like this.
betterruins:Then take the map and let yo: Then take the map and let your own judgement guide you. Some places are better understood in silence than in stories.
betterruins:Then you are smarter than yo:
Then you are smarter than you look. Lesser adventurers would have disappeared into that ruin and not returned, blinded by the glimmer of gold, like so many before them.

Feel free to stick around here and browse my wares instead. That way, you won’t go home empty-handed after all.
There are plenty of stories. They gather like dirt on boots. Listening to them is certainly safer than checking them.
betterruins:There are whispers, traveler: There are whispers, traveler. Tales passed from one sun-scorched tongue to the next - of a place far beneath the dunes. An ancient tomb, where four trade empires once crossed paths and secrets were locked away in silence. It's not on any common map... but I may possess something rare.
betterruins:There is one. But it holds n: There is one. But it holds no more certainty than the others.
betterruins:There were rumors about the: There were rumors about the existence of one place. Distant and large. So distant that speaking of it is already an achievement. People wanted to influence something that, as is customary, cannot really be influenced. They wanted to muffle... or even push away... the screech of metal in the middle of the day, and the feeling of rust in the air. But the world doesn't like it much when its manifestations are silenced.
This had better be worth it...
betterruins:This is definitely useful kn: This is definitely useful knowledge, thank you very much.
betterruins:Very well. Take the map, and: Very well. Take the map, and may your steps be careful where the sun once burned brightest.
betterruins:Well, thank you in turn! For: Well, thank you in turn! For humouring me, and getting me this scythe. This thing’s much heavier than it looks, and I could use someone of your faculties to carry it back to my farmhouse when I tire of trading. But that’s nowhere in the foreseeable future! Let’s worry about right now; all those gears that are weighing you down. Come take a look at my wares, I’ll gladly help you lighten those pockets.
betterruins:Why, thank you for entertain: Why, thank you for entertaining my request. Remember to stock up on food before you leave, it won’t do you any good to go prospecting on an empty stomach.
betterruins:Yes, but not exactly payment: Yes, but not exactly payment. A confirmation of your abilities. Show that you can handle good metal - bring me an iron pickaxe you forged yourself. If you're going there, better not go without purpose or craftsmanship.
betterruins:Yes, knowledge and items you: Yes, knowledge and items you'll need there. Considering the different rumors, the danger seems to still live there. You'll need equipment that can withstand an unexpected strike. You'll need fire - it doesn't burn willingly there, so take enough torches. Also - support, something to brace yourself against if the ground trembles. And medicine - absolutely. The pain from those events has most likely remained there, and the place will gladly share it with any visitor. Perhaps even with the first visitor...
betterruins:Yes, my appreciation of natu: Yes, my appreciation of nature doesn’t end at all that sticks out of the ground, but my skills don’t lend themselves particularly well to working metal. This might be my only opportunity to see something like this, let alone own it for myself! And I don’t intend to squander it if you’re interested in that ruin. Trader’s mindset, I suppose. I just can't help myself! Speaking of trade, are you buying?
betterruins:You probably wander the worl: [BR Quest] You probably wander the world a lot. Heard many stories?
betterruins:[BR Quest] Do you have any t: [BR Quest] Do you have any tips for preserving food?

lore-agitatedregards-piece1:
Ripley, this has to stop. I understand that you think your projects are important but I would think keeping the House Head happy and fed is quite important in its own right. In all of our best interests, in fact! I just watched Goldfinch fire another serf after he offered them grapes deemed too small. A choking hazard. There’s not many servants left to take the fall for me before I end up having to present the fruits and vegetables in person.

I keep reaching for the saltpeter to fashion my fertilizer and finding the vessels empty. When you use the last of something, you put in an order for more. That is how things work around here. I understand this is your first time as research head, but we cannot afford for you to make these mistakes. I spent years training in the Derabul academy to trim hedges and sprout flowers, never to grow crops, let alone enough produce to feed the entire staff. And I will admit I have dreamt more than once of working on the Askannon orchards instead. But regardless I have taken on my new duties swimmingly. Why can’t you do the same?

The leatherworker, bless her soul, accused me of having used too much! Yet my fields have never looked worse, and I know my green fingers are not to blame. Whatever you’re doing down there had better be worth the trouble you’re causing up in the House by so carelessly draining our reagents. I have put in another order of niter, twice the size as usual, and I implore you to leave some for the rest of us this time.

With agitated regards,
Basira Qamar,
Head Horticulturist of House Goldfinch

___NEWPAGE___
lore-authoritativecopy-piece1:
This document constitutes a faithful and binding record of the trade agreement entered into by the Svanmarck Estate and House Goldfinch, under the eye of the Crown of Undland and with the assent of its appointed Arbiter, to govern matters of passage, access, and non-interference between the two houses.

House Svanmarck affirms its sole authority over the construction, maintenance, and operation of roads, canals, and other regional infrastructure within Goldfinch lands and holdings.

House Goldfinch is granted permanent and preferential access to all Svanmarck-maintained infrastructure required for the transport of goods, materials, and persons between Goldfinch holdings and points of trade.

House Goldfinch and its interests shall not need to pay tolls on roads on its own territory. Access to Svanmarck infrastructure shall not otherwise be withheld, restricted, or made conditional beyond maintenance fees as fixed at the time of signing, except by direct sanction of the Crown of Undland.

House Svanmarck shall ensure reasonable maintenance and timely repair of said infrastructure where it services Goldfinch routes, and shall not delay or neglect such maintenance for the purpose of leverage, pressure, or advantage.

House Svanmarck affirms non-interference in the internal operations, extraction, and trade practices of House Goldfinch, and shall not employ its control of infrastructure to influence, hinder, or extract additional concessions from Goldfinch interests.

House Goldfinch recognizes the Svanmarck Estate as the sole authority over regional infrastructure, and agrees not to construct or commission competing roads, canals, or transit works within Goldfinch territory.

This agreement is witnessed and sealed under authority of the Crown of Undland, signed threefold by representatives of their respective noble houses.
lore-brickworkerslament-piece1:
Everything automated through these locusts and helpers and the occasional eidolon, but still we must remain at our stations. To provide our “expertise”, but with no involvement in the process itself…
No, we are mere scapegoats for when the contraptions invariably fail. We are given tasks that are insultingly simple, yet leave us entirely responsible. It’s you who activated the automaton, so it’s you who are at fault for its failures.

I think I would have preferred if they had simply let us go, but instead we sit around waiting. Waiting for the inevitable shift the locusts break down again. Waiting to take the blame for their failure. Once in a blue moon, they are unable to find a brickworker to fault, and they seek answers among the engineers. I’d heard how those meetings go, once, in passing. Every shortcoming blamed on Jonas Falx, and in the same breath they claim still that their designs are entirely their own.
Are these engineers so proud that they refuse to consider the possibility their artifice needs improvement, that their imitations are imperfect? I came from a proud line of masons, myself, but I take pride in stonework that can stand the test of time, not whatever novel trinket most impresses Gage Goldfinch.

I must remain in their good graces, though. During that same meeting I learned the Calix is nearing completion, and that soon we will all be living lives free of worry. So I will clench my teeth a little longer and turn on the automatons at the start of all my shifts, and pray to God that they keep working, so that I may keep working here in turn.
lore-doubts-piece1:
Doubts 1 / Commoner
Why now? 

Do not misunderstand me, I am grateful we can at least have this.
But why now? For many years I have dreamt of cooperation at this scale. 

Why did it take the Rot to unite us? 
Is it only because we now stand together against a common foe?
If hatred for an Other is the only thing that will let us overcome hatred for another, then…
I pray that, if the Grand Machine works, we do not return to our old ways.
And that if it fails, we stay united until the bitter end.___NEWPAGE___
lore-doubts-piece2:
Doubts 2 / Blackguard
I stood at the gates for years leaning on my trusty poleax. A bardiche, a terrific weapon. She’d be certain to strike fear into the hearts of those taking shelter, at least those who retain their sight still. I miss her weight in my hands. How I wish I’d had room to swing her down here!

In truth, more than anything I miss the distance she put between me and those ne’er-do-wells. I used to envy the bowmen. They never had to see the fruits of their labour up close. Now that I’m stuck in these tight tunnels with nothing but a shortsword, though, I understand how good I had it with my polearm.___NEWPAGE___
lore-doubts-piece3:
Doubts 3 / Malefactor
Is it wrong of me to wish suffering upon others?
These… malefactors, we call them. People who have lied and stolen and murdered.
I understand why they wear the masks now.
Had I recognized him, I would have sent him to God, myself.
Instead, I am left hoping that they all meet their end on the surface, him among them.___NEWPAGE___
lore-doubts-piece4:
Doubts 4 / Hunter
I think I shot a person today.

It was hard to tell due to the Rot. I was seeking quarry at the perimeter of the encroaching disease, trying to bring in what meat I could before it was lost. 

Most quarry runs toward you, away from the plagued lands, choosing a swift death over slow decay. It’s risky but you can’t argue with the results. I don’t think I’ve ever heard one ask me to put it out of its misery before, though.___NEWPAGE___
lore-doubts-piece5:
Doubts 5 / Clockmaker
The Prima Materia is beyond even my understanding.
And I would consider myself quite learned. 
I wish I could be happier for it. I always enjoyed learning new things. 

Instead I have never felt more like a bumbling fool. Like I did when I first set foot in the University. The world seemed so small then, in retrospect. Now the sheer amount of possibilities overwhelms me, and I would not know where to begin.

I will leave it to Jonas Falx to figure out the particulars, as most of my peers have, and work diligently to provide the parts he requests.___NEWPAGE___
lore-doubts-piece6:
Doubts 6 / Tailor
Over, under, draw it through…

I’ve seen a great many adopt mantras in these trying times. Me, I already have one. It has stayed with me through many years of weaving.

Over, under, draw it through…

I refuse to let my hands idle. There’s always someone in need of warmth, in both senses of the word. I am grateful I am able to provide it to them.

Over, under, draw it through…

And when this all blows over, I hope that when they remember this place, they think of the warm fabric upon their skin and not the cold stone beneath their feet.___NEWPAGE___
lore-hopeandisaiahsledgers-piece1:
Day 1. Faulkner has ordered closure of all canal ingress points and instructed us to maintain order among the detained.

Approximately 43 detainees inside the reservoir at lockdown moment:
- 17 labourers
- 11 traders/boatmen
- 5 accompanying guards
- 6 miscellaneous travelers
- 4 children

Per Faulkner’s directive:
- No one exits until a cure is found.
- Anyone showing signs of lesions or fever is to be separated to the sick zone in the lower reservoir.
- No gatherings larger than six persons without warden supervision.

Rations have been seized, catalogued, and redistributed. Perishables - primarily fish from one highly disgruntled merchant - will last the first week if shared equitably. Merchant protested but complied after formal promise of compensation. Let us hope the quarantine resolves swiftly. 

Drafted by Isaiah
Confirmed by Hope___NEWPAGE___
lore-hopeandisaiahsledgers-piece2:
Day 7. Spirits are uneasy. Individuals demand answers we cannot give.

Two attempted to bribe passage through the south sluice. Sluice is jammed anyway - collapse from Faulkner’s blast. Both offenders placed in restricted quarters for twelve hours; released afterward with warning.

Faulkner requests written updates only. Claims he is “concentrating”.
We have asked for clear medical procedure and received nothing in return as of yet.

Standing water in the lower reservoir sick zone has already turned foul. Several of the initially isolated labourers have succumbed to disease overnight. We have begun herding detainees to sleep on the walkways to reduce exposure.

Child of the traveler Roland displays fever but no lesions. 
Roland pleaded for exemption; request granted on grounds that forced separation would incite further unrest. Both have been moved to the sick zone.

Drafted by Isaiah
Confirmed by Hope___NEWPAGE___
lore-hopeandisaiahsledgers-piece3:
Day 13. Fatigue increasing among both detainees and wardens.

Of the original 43 detained, 22 remain alive. Most recent losses occurred overnight in the sick zone.

The dead are piling up below, but with limited ventilation we cannot safely burn them. The sick that are still capable are ordered to move them to the collapsed tunnel until a permanent solution is found.

Three labourers attempted to bypass the walkway cordon during the night. Claimed they sought fresher air. Returned to designated area and reprimanded. 

The late Roland’s daughter asked us whether he would “wake once the air is clearer”. Informed this was a question for Faulkner.

Ration supplies remain stable, albeit at reduced allotment. With fewer individuals to feed, current stores may last much longer than projected.

First lesions observed on one of the accompanying guards previously assessed as healthy.
Isolated to the sick zone.

Still no medical procedure from Faulkner.

Drafted by Isaiah
Confirmed by Hope___NEWPAGE___
lore-hopeandisaiahsledgers-piece4:
Day 24? Day 25? The record must continue.

Population estimate: Nine remain in varying stages of decay.
Several are unable to stand. Most do not speak. Those who still breathe do so shallowly.
Movement between walkways has ceased. The sick zone is silent.

Faulkner has not responded to our last reports. We believe he has relocated deeper into the tunnels to continue his work.

Hope is… resting.
Their sight has fully left them, though they still turn their head when I speak.
My own condition is manageable. Previous attempts to doff my armor have resulted in torn skin.
Rot progressing along forearm and ribs. Pain intermittent.
Alas. The ledger is not for complaints.

Rations still adequate. Hardly consumed. No reason to maintain allotment schedule.

There is little more to report. Procedures remain in place with no-one left to enforce them upon. 
Still we hold our posts. It is what is expected of us. We have given everything we have to this duty and now there is nothing left.

I will play for Hope. On Faulkner’s piano. I will play a piece we both remember. I will burn it into my muscle memory if I need to, that I might still play it when I lose my own sight. And I pray to the Gods that this is the last thing we hear before the black sick takes our minds from us, too.

Drafted by Isaiah___NEWPAGE___
lore-panopticonletters-piece1:
Even with all these folks suffering alongside me I’ve never felt more lonely.

The wardens see to that. Any attempt at fraternizing will be met with accusations of spreading the plague first and accusations of staging a rebellion second.  And it’ll see both parties made into a display for the rest.

I only hope the black sick takes us all quickly.___NEWPAGE___
lore-panopticonletters-piece2:
What is this mistreatment?!

I am Faris Hussain, heir to the throne of Derabul. I have come to expect better than this!
On a routine mercantile journey to share the finest silks with the world I find myself led down into a damp dark crevice.

My silks have been torn and turned to cleaning rags. Horrible! These brutish labourers would not know value if it stared them in the face. Yet I am stuck with them here. The lazarettos I have visited at least possessed some semblance of privacy, so what is this claim of quarantine? It is nonsense. I will have a word with these enforcers about granting me exit. They are certain to understand. Even if they do not, they will understand the wealth that awaits them for making exceptions for the exceptional.___NEWPAGE___
